questions.stem: Internal energy of a substance is the sum of:

options.text: The kinetic energy of the substance as a whole
The kinetic energy and potential energy of all its particles
Only the potential energy stored in bonds between particles
The temperature and pressure of the substance

questions.explanation: Internal energy is the total of the kinetic energy (due to particle movement) and potential energy (due to bonds/forces between particles) of all the particles in a substance.

questions.stem: When a solid is heated but does not change state, its internal energy increases mainly because:

options.text: The potential energy between particles increases
The particles vibrate faster, increasing their kinetic energy
The mass of the substance increases

questions.explanation: When a solid is heated without changing state, the particles vibrate faster and their kinetic energy increases. This causes the temperature to rise. The potential energy remains roughly the same since no bonds are being broken.
